text: The whole community of Israel set out from Elim and came to the wilderness of Sin, which lies between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they left Egypt.
In the wilderness the whole community of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron.

versions.text: And in the wilderness the whole community grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew specifies "the whole congregation of the children of Israel"; the identifier "of Israel" has been dropped. Removing the sentence-initial "And" and placing "In the wilderness" first also reads more smoothly aloud.

text: The Israelites said to them, "If only we had died by the LORD's hand in Egypt, where we sat beside pots of meat and ate all the bread we wanted! But you brought us out into this wilderness to starve this whole assembly to death."

Then the LORD said to Moses, "I am going to rain down bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test them, to see whether they will follow my instruction or not.
On the sixth day they are to gather twice as much as on the other days, and prepare it."
So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, "This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of Egypt,
and in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we, that you should grumble against us?"

Moses also said, "The LORD will give you meat to eat in the evening and all the bread you want in the morning, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we? Your grumbling is not against us but against the LORD."
Then Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the whole community of Israel: 'Come before the LORD, for he has heard your grumbling.'"
While Aaron was speaking to the whole community of Israel, they turned toward the wilderness, and there was the glory of the LORD appearing in the cloud.
The LORD said to Moses,
"I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them: 'At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.'"
That evening quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew all around the camp.
When the layer of dew lifted, there on the surface of the wilderness lay something thin and flaky, fine as frost on the ground.

versions.text: When the layer of dew lifted, there on the desert floor lay something thin and flaky, fine as frost on the ground.
versions.explanation: The same Hebrew word (midbar) is rendered "wilderness" throughout the chapter (vv. 1, 2, 3, 10, 32); switching to "desert floor" here breaks the consistency a listener depends on.

text: When the Israelites saw it, they said to one another, "What is it?"—for they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, "It is the bread the LORD has given you to eat." [Footnote: The Hebrew words behind "What is it?" sound like the name manna given in verse 31.]

versions.text: When the Israelites saw it, they said to one another, "What is it?"—for they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, "It is the bread the LORD has given you to eat.
versions.explanation: The wordplay between the question man hu and the name manna in v. 31 is invisible in English; a brief footnote preserves it for hearers. (Note also that the closing quotation mark is missing at the end of Moses' words.)

text: This is what the LORD has commanded: Each of you is to gather as much as you need—an omer for every person in your tent."
The Israelites did so, and some gathered much, some little.
But when they measured it by the omer, the one who gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who gathered little had no lack. Each had gathered as much as he needed.
Then Moses said to them, "No one is to keep any of it until morning."
But some paid no attention to Moses; they kept part of it until morning, and it was full of maggots and began to stink. So Moses was angry with them.
Morning by morning they gathered it, each as much as he needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
On the sixth day they gathered twice as much—two omers for each person—and the leaders of the community came and reported it to Moses.

He said to them, "This is what the LORD has said: Tomorrow is to be a day of rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to boil, and save what is left, keeping it until morning."
So they saved it until morning, as Moses commanded, and it did not stink or get maggots in it.
"Eat it today," Moses said, "because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find any of it in the field.
Six days you are to gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be none."
Even so, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather it, but they found nothing.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to keep my commands and my instructions?
Understand that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Everyone is to stay where he is on the seventh day; no one is to leave his place."
So the people rested on the seventh day.
The house of Israel called it manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.

Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded: Take a full omer of it and keep it for the generations to come, so they can see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of Egypt."

versions.text: Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded: Take an omerful of it and keep it for the generations to come, so they can see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of Egypt."
versions.explanation: "Omerful" is an unusual coinage that stumbles when read aloud; "a full omer" renders melo ha-omer accurately and speaks more naturally.

text: So Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put a full omer of manna in it. Then place it before the LORD, to be kept for the generations to come."

versions.text: So Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put an omerful of manna in it. Then place it before the LORD, to be kept for the generations to come."
versions.explanation: Same as v. 32: "a full omer" is clearer and more natural for oral reading than "an omerful," and keeps the two verses consistent.

text: So Aaron placed it before the testimony, to be kept, as the LORD commanded Moses. [Footnote: That is, before the tablets of the covenant, which were kept in the ark.]

versions.text: So Aaron put it before the ark of the covenant law, to be kept, as the LORD commanded Moses.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads simply "before the testimony"; "the ark of" is added content. Rendering the term literally with an explanatory footnote avoids importing information the text does not state.

text: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where people lived; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
An omer is a tenth of an ephah.
